correctness.rationale: For an edge U,V set A=U∩V and B=U+V. Any common neighbor W not containing A has two distinct (k−1)-spaces W∩U and W∩V spanning W, so lies in B. A star-only vertex intersects B precisely in A and is therefore nonadjacent to any top-only vertex. The star and top extend the edge, have sizes greater than q+1, and are its only maximal cliques. Their common vertices are exactly the projective line of the pencil. For an empty trace on at most three vertices, fix a (k−2)-space; there are L_q(n−k+2) potential star centers through it and at most 3(q+1) are forbidden. One-positive labels exclude at most two hyperplanes of the positive vertex, fewer than L_q(k). An all-positive trace requires a clique, and on a triangle the two-positive traces are all possible exactly when the third vertex is not in the pair's pencil. Nonpencil triangles have a unique containing clique, so a shattered four-set cannot realize its triple-positive trace in addition to the all-positive trace. Shattered triples exist because star quotients have dimension at least three. In a putative depth-four online tree the second query on the positive branch must differ from the root (otherwise its negative child is impossible). At most two concepts survive the double positive, not enough for the four suffix leaves. For counting edges, each U selects an A⊂U and B⊃U, with q other vertices per pencil; nonpencil triples are counted once via projective noncollinear triples in one star or top. Pencil triples determine their pencil by any pair. Every edge extends within its star outside the pencil, proving purity.
